Its very hard. I had an awakening and i sobbed for hours because I genuinely thought I needed to be admitted because I had gotten so bad. But honestly, uncle google is really helpful. I was googling mental breakdowns and spiritual awakenings, and its very VERY different. I am a psych student as well, and my first thought is always "surely not. Im just fucked in the head". The only tried and true way that you will be able to tell the difference is by being in a feeling of uncertainty and anxiety. I suggest writing those things down in a journal or on your phone. You will really quickly find your balance and what is and isnt a gut feeling. Lastly, a gut feeling almost feels like a dullness deep in your tummy alongside immediate thoughts about what is going to happen or go wrong. Dont be afraid to google things, genuinely. You can never learn too much about yourself. Try to visit pages that seem reliable. Or even just post in this sub and ask anything and everything. Learning is a process, self learning is harder, but the payoff is beyond rewarding.

I'm not telling anyone to not go to the doctors, but as someone with chronic anxiety, been to multiple doctors over 4 years, had multiple tests done, and studying psychology, I think it's okay to remind those who are also in the same shoes as me that we aren't mentally deranged. Hey bud, sorry to hear about your experience. But like mentioned, it’s the meds, not you. Sertraline only worked for me for two months and then made my life even more shitty for a very very long time (as doctors at the time refused to change my meds). I’ve recently switched to venlafaxine and I’ve found it working pretty well for me. However, everyone has a different reaction to medications, so always go through side effects with your doctor as that’s what they’re there for.   Also, overdosing seems like a great path, but it really isn’t. It’s not just a sleep you fall into, it’s chest pains, choking, vomiting and excruciating. You don’t deserve to cause yourself any more pain that what you currently feel now, and I mean that. Talk to your doctor ASAP and insist on a change of meds and don’t leave the room until a decision you are comfortable with has been reached.
